page: The Vultr voc-m-1c-8gb-50s-amd is an entry-level memory-optimized instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute series. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU with simultaneous multithreading disabled. The configuration integrates 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for workloads requiring higher memory capacity than standard compute configurations without provisioning superfluous CPU capacity. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address. The CPU feature set includes AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Benchmark results demonstrate contrasting performance attributes defined strictly by the single-core execution boundary. In single-threaded execution, the instance performs solidly, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1999.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2896.39, both placing in the upper quartile among tested servers. Data compression routines also reflect steady single-thread performance, delivering 27.17 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 11.19 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the single-core allocation, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 1961.0 and total PassMark CPU output registering at 2424.5.

System memory and I/O throughput benchmarks indicate lower operational boundaries for high-bandwidth data transfers. Large block uncached memory bandwidth registers at 22.42 GB/sec for read operations and 20.94 GB/sec for write operations. Networked application benchmarks mirror these hardware constraints, recording static web serving throughput at 1.44 GB/sec and Redis SET performance at 1.96 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning inference, the small 135M model generates 86.78 tokens per second, but medium and large model benchmarks are constrained by hardware scope.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the instance offers balanced utility for tasks requiring dedicated single-core stability and a larger memory envelope without the operational expense of multi-core plans. Tradeoffs center on the absence of parallel core execution and moderate memory bandwidth. The voc-m-1c-8gb-50s-amd is technically aligned with lightweight in-memory caching nodes, single-threaded backend services, staging environments, small Redis deployments, and low-traffic web applications.
description: The Vultr voc-m-1c-8gb-50s-amd is an entry-tier memory-optimized instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 1 dedicated vCPU powered by an AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 8.0 GB of RAM to deliver an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation. Storage is provided via a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, supported by 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmark data exhibits solid single-core processing capabilities, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 1999.0 and a stress-ng metric of 2896.39. In contrast, aggregate parallel throughput and memory bandwidth remain modest due to the physical constraint of a single CPU core, as shown by a PassMark CPU score of 2424.5 and memory read bandwidth of 22.42 GB/sec. This hardware profile is best matched with low-concurrency workloads that need reliable memory space, such as dedicated in-memory caches, background utility workers, and lightweight application services.
